terms.explain: The Quran as a written, bound book, in its established order.
terms.forDevs: Used when the properties of the written representation matter: rasm, layout, pages, lines and marks.

terms.explain: A principal unit of the structure of the Quran, made up of ordered ayahs, with a name and a known place in the order of the mushaf.
terms.forDevs: Used as the principal unit for organising the text and for attaching ayahs and surah-level data.

terms.explain: A unit of the Quranic text falling within a surah and having determined boundaries. Its number, and some of its boundaries, may differ from one ayah numbering system to another.
terms.forDevs: Used as the basic unit for referring to the Quranic text, and for attaching translations, tafsir, recitations, analyses and other data to a specific place in the Quran.

terms.explain: The formula «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم» with which the surahs open, except surah al-Tawbah. It carries rulings and differences bound up with ayah counting.
terms.forDevs: Used to identify the basmalah and to represent its position and its relation to the surah and to the ayah numbering system.

terms.explain: One of the ways of reciting the Quran, attributed to one of the imams of the qiraat, from which the riwayahs and tariqs branch.
terms.forDevs: Represents the top level of the qiraat model and ties together the riwayahs, the tariqs and the texts bound to them.

terms.explain: What is attributed to a transmitter from an imam of a qiraah, such as the riwayah of Hafs from Asim.
terms.forDevs: Used to state which riwayah a text, a mushaf, a recording or a dataset follows.

terms.explain: One to whom a transmission from an imam of a qiraah is attributed.
terms.forDevs: Used to represent the person a `riwayah` is bound to.

terms.explain: The way the words of the Quran are written: which letters are written and which omitted or added, and where words are joined or kept apart.
terms.forDevs: Used as a classification stating which rasm a text, a mushaf or a dataset is written in, so that search, comparison and rendering branch on it; and it keeps the layer of the rasm distinct from the font, the layout and the drawn glyphs.

terms.explain: A mark fixing a letter's vowel, its absence or its doubling: fathah, dammah, kasrah, sukun and shaddah.
terms.forDevs: Used as the parent of the dabt marks that determine how the letter itself is pronounced.

terms.explain: Marks a doubled letter: the first, vowelless, is merged into the second and the two are pronounced as one stressed letter.
terms.forDevs: Used as a value of harakah, so that a letter's pronunciation is read from it in analysis, rendering and teaching rather than from the shape of the mark.

terms.explain: Stopping the recitation at a place in the text according to the rules of stopping and starting.
terms.forDevs: Represents the general concept of stopping, while `waqf_mark` represents the printed signs that point to it.

terms.explain: The circle separating one ayah from the next. It is placed at the ayah's end and, in most mushafs, carries its number.
terms.forDevs: Used to mark an ayah's boundary in the written text; it is the sign from which a renderer or an analyser reads where an ayah ends and what its number is.

terms.explain: The discipline of delivering the letters of the Quran from their points of articulation and giving them their due properties and rulings.
terms.forDevs: Used as the discipline that tajwid rules, rulings and colour annotations belong to, so that a rule in an engine or a dictionary is attributed to it.

terms.explain: What is due in delivering a letter before the letter that follows it, or at a sukun or a hamzah: izhar, idgham, iqlab, ikhfa, madd, qalqalah, tafkhim or tarqiq, as the rules of tajwid settle it at a given place in the text.
terms.forDevs: Used as the parent of the rulings of tajwid and the holder of their registry, so that the places in the text where a ruling falls are attributed to it, and a particular ruling is named by a row of the registry rather than by a free name that differs from one engine to another.
